summary: VERIFY ROUND, ALL BY MEASUREMENT: 33 mutations applied one at a time to the staged bytes, each run as `./gradlew :sequencer:test --tests InvariantsTest --tests InvariantsAcrossChainsTest` (19 tests) with the result XML deleted before every run so a compile failure cannot be read as a survival. TR-A IS FIXED: `inherited.merge(..., Math::max)` -> `Math::min` at Invariants.java:254 now FAILS aTakeoversTWOChainsAreCheckedACROSSTheirJoin (the two-delta predecessor makes the fold report the successor's resume at 8 as a `gap`), and the clean checkout is green at 182/182. TR-B IS FIXED: dropping the defensive `Math.max(from, ...)` at Invariants.java:118 now FAILS theHIGHWATERMARKNEVERGOESBACKWARDSAfterARewind, and its `containsExactly("I2")` is the RIGHT assertion, not `contains` -- the mutant's mark falls back to 4 and the third delta at 6 becomes a phantom `gap`, which only an exact assertion sees. TR-C IS FIXED (the baseline now calls the shared `start`), and I AGREE the redrive budget is an equivalent mutant here: 8->1 and 8->0 both survive all 19, but CommitLogSealWriteTest:119/239 and LocalSequencerTest:254-271 constrain the budget under real contention, so it is not globally unconstrained. TR-D: FIXED_CLOCK -> systemUTC() still survives all 19, correctly disclosed on M4.25 rather than fixed here. NO REGRESSION: the transitive hop (discard the recursion's result, and depth>1000 -> depth>0) dies on offsetsAreInheritedTRANSITIVELY; both first-seal scans die SEPARATELY (fold scan alone and checkLink scan alone each fail aSECONDSeal AND theFOLDStops); the `gap` arm, `< from` -> `< from - 1`, `firstAncestorWithDeltas -> 0`, the I1/I5/chain arms, the no-CONTINUE arm, the unsealed-predecessor arm, the `continuedAt` arm, the prevSeq arm, the never-opened walk-back and the seal-bounded fold break all die on exactly the test that names them. ALL 19 TESTS ARE NON-VACUOUS: every one of them is the sole or joint killer of at least one mutation, and 12 of the 19 kill a mutation NO other test kills. The takeover fixture's counts(6)+counts(2)/isEqualTo(8) edit weakened nothing: production mutations open(prevEpoch,0), open(0,0) and skipping the predecessor's SEAL are each still killed by that same test. Findings below are three surviving mutations OUTSIDE the arms the M4.19 row claims, plus one unreproducible number; none blocks.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: replacing readChain's page loop (Invariants.java:349-352) with an unconditional `return out;` -- the checker reads only the FIRST list page of a chain and silently ignores the rest -- leaves all 19 invariant tests green. No fixture builds a chain longer than 5 entries, so `nextStartAfter` is always empty and the outer loop never runs twice. The companion mutation (page size 1000 -> 1, forcing many pages) also survives with all 19 green, which shows the loop is CORRECT today; what is unconstrained is that it runs at all. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SAME BLIND SPOT `SmallPageStore` WAS WRITTEN FOR, in this same package, whose javadoc records the identical measurement against `CommitLog.recover` ('every fixture in the suite holds fewer objects than the 1000 `CommitLog` asks for, so `nextStartAfter` is always empty ... Measured -- the mutation survived the whole sequencer suite'). `Invariants.readChain` reintroduces it with the decorator sitting one file away.
findings.failure_scenario: A term that commits more than one list page of entries -- reachable inside a single leader's term at a seconds-scale flush interval, and exactly the history length M4.8's checkpoints exist for -- has its chain truncated by the checker. Every I1, I2, `gap` and I5 violation past the page boundary is invisible, and because `checkChain` returns an empty list for a chain it did not fully read (M4.22's defect, one step worse) M4.13's seeded sweep would report those seeds CLEAN. ⚠️ REMEDY MEASURED, and it costs nothing: changing ONE existing fixture to `Invariants.checkChain(new SmallPageStore(store, 2), PREFIX, 1)` in anEntryBEYONDASealIsReportedAsI5 makes the truncation mutation FAIL that test -- verified by applying both edits together and reverting. No 1001-entry fixture is needed.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: `inherited.merge(new RunKey(run.key().indexId(), 0), ...)` at Invariants.java:254 -- the cross-boundary fold keyed by INDEX ONLY, discarding the partition -- leaves all 19 green. Cause is the fixture: `counts(n)` and `delta(...)` both hard-code `new RunKey(A, 0)`, so every chain in both test classes carries exactly ONE stream and the checker's per-stream separation is never exercised across a boundary. (The mirror mutations that drop the indexId from the running mark DO die, at 10 and 6 kills, because A is a non-zero UUID -- so it is specifically the partition dimension, and specifically the inherited half, that is unpinned.)
findings.failure_scenario: A checker that conflates the partitions of one index when folding a predecessor's deltas assigns partition 1 the high-water mark of partition 0. In a real multi-partition chain -- the only kind this system writes, RunKey being (indexId, partitionId) -- every failover then reports a phantom I2 or `gap` for every partition but the lowest, and M4.13's sweep attributes checker artefacts to production as violating seeds. It would also mask the converse: a real reassignment in partition 1 hidden behind partition 0's higher mark. Nothing in the tree distinguishes the two.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: narrowing the I5 arm at Invariants.java:107 from `if (seal != null)` to `if (seal != null && seal.sequence() + 1 == e.sequence())` -- report only the FIRST entry past the seal, not every one -- leaves all 19 green. anEntryBEYONDASealIsReportedAsI5 asserts `containsExactly("I5")`, which LOOKS like a count assertion, but its fixture has exactly one post-seal entry, so the cardinality of the I5 arm is unconstrained. This is the same shape as the TR-B finding the author accepted: the arm still fires, but the number and per-entry detail it reports do not.
findings.failure_scenario: A fenced writer that appends several deltas past the barrier -- the multi-entry case aSECONDSeal builds in epoch 1 but never checks epoch 1 for -- is reported as ONE I5 violation instead of one per discarded entry. M4.13's sweep pins exact violation counts (the argument the monotonicity fixture is built on), so a seed producing a 5-entry post-seal suffix would be indistinguishable from one producing a 1-entry suffix, and an operator reading the report cannot tell how much was acknowledged past the barrier. One extra `put` in the existing fixture plus `containsExactly("I5", "I5")` closes it.

findings.summary: THREE DIFFERENT UNREPRODUCIBLE TEST COUNTS, all added by this commit, none matching the staged tree. backlog.md:272 (M4.25) says FIXED_CLOCK survives with 'all 18 invariant tests green' -- this commit ships 19. backlog.md:270 (M4.23) says the neverOpened weakening leaves 'all 180 sequencer tests green'. InvariantsTest.java:172 says the Math.max was unconstrained 'across all 181 tests'. MEASURED on the staged bytes: `./gradlew :sequencer:test` is 178 tests, and 182 only when the four UNTRACKED CommitProtocolSimulationTest cases are present -- so 180 and 181 are counts of a working tree that a fresh clone does not have. That is the very objection this file's own comment at InvariantsAcrossChainsTest.java:342 makes ('the only thing in the tree that noticed was an UNTRACKED M4.20 file, which is no coverage at all').
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader re-runs the stated experiment to decide whether M4.23 and M4.25 are still real, gets 19 and 178 rather than 18, 180 and 181, and cannot tell whether the arm became constrained since, whether the suite shrank, or whether the number was measured against files that were never committed. The M4.12 row already argues that a count in prose is stale the moment a round adds a test, and here the same commit both adds the test and writes the stale number. No gate reads these numbers, so nothing will ever correct them.
